primary_claim: Adding an auxiliary self-modeling (predicting one's own internal activations) objective to supervised classification training consistently reduces measured model complexity (lower RLCT, narrower final-layer weight distribution) across three tasks and two modalities, without significantly hurting task performance.

effect.metric: RLCT (Local Learning Coefficient) and final-layer weight distribution width
effect.value: complexity reduction scales with the weight placed on the self-modeling loss, without significantly affecting task performance

stated_future_work: further exploring the potential effects of self-modeling on cooperation as an alignment approach
limitations_stated: experiments employ small networks on simple classification tasks, so it is unclear whether the effect scales to larger models, more complex contexts, or more agentic set-ups (e.g. multiagent RL)
self-modeling could inadvertently boost capabilities in risky ways, e.g. heightened self-awareness enabling more competent manipulation of users
if self-modeling causes sufficiently complex models to become conscious, there are unresolved moral patienthood concerns
quote: Across three different classification tasks, we consistently found that adding a self-modeling mechanism to neural networks significantly reduced their complexity
